title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and superstitions that define the Auburn Family, from rolling the oaks to the pre-game eagle flight.

cards.title: Rolling Toomer's Corner
cards.subtitle: A Snowy Celebration of Victory
cards.notes: Toss rolls of toilet paper into the oak trees at the intersection of College and Magnolia after every major Auburn win.
cards.short_summary: Auburn fans celebrate athletic victories by covering the iconic Toomer's Oaks in toilet paper, a tradition dating back to the 1960s.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition of rolling Toomer's Corner began in the 1960s when employees at Toomer's Drugs threw telegraph ticker tape into the trees to signal away-game wins.
cards.source_title: Traditions - Rolling Toomer's Corner - Auburn Tigers
cards.access_notes: Open to the public after victories; participants should bring their own rolls of toilet paper.

cards.title: The Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: The Original Gameday Procession
cards.notes: Line Donahue Drive two hours before kickoff to high-five players and coaches as they walk from the Athletics Complex to the stadium.
cards.short_summary: Thousands of fans line the street to cheer the football team into Jordan-Hare Stadium, a tradition that began in the 1960s.
cards.evidence_claim: Tiger Walk began in the 1960s when kids would walk up the street to meet the team for autographs; it now draws over 20,000 fans for major games.
cards.access_notes: Occurs two hours before every home game along South Donahue Drive.

cards.title: The War Eagle Flight
cards.subtitle: A Majestic Pre-Game Ritual
cards.notes: Watch a golden or bald eagle circle the stadium and land at midfield as the crowd chants 'War Eagle' before kickoff.
cards.short_summary: A live eagle from the Southeastern Raptor Center performs a free flight over the crowd before home football games.
cards.evidence_claim: The eagle flight is a unique Auburn tradition where a raptor circles the entire stadium before landing, symbolizing the school's battle cry.
cards.access_notes: Visible to ticket holders inside Jordan-Hare Stadium before home games.

cards.title: Hey Day
cards.subtitle: The Friendliest Day on the Plains
cards.notes: Wear a provided nametag and greet everyone you pass with a friendly 'Hey' to promote campus unity.
cards.short_summary: An annual tradition since 1947 where students and faculty wear nametags to foster a welcoming environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Hey Day was established in 1947 to help World War II veterans transition back to campus and feel recognized by the student body.
cards.source_title: Auburn Tradition: The History of Hey Day
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; nametags are distributed at various campus locations.

cards.title: Cater Callouts
cards.subtitle: Public Membership Announcements
cards.notes: Gather at the back steps of Cater Hall to hear the names of new members selected for major campus organizations.
cards.short_summary: A student-led tradition where organizations announce their new rosters from the steps of the historic Katherine Cooper Cater Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Callouts are a sacred tradition unique to Auburn students where groups like the cheerleading team and SGA announce new members publicly.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the evenings following organization tryouts or elections.

cards.title: The Seal Superstition
cards.subtitle: Don't Step on the Curse
cards.notes: Avoid stepping on the university seal embedded in the sidewalk in front of Langdon Hall to ensure you graduate on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus legend warns that stepping on the seal will prevent graduation in four years and curse your future family.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend says stepping on the seal means you won't graduate in four years, won't find true love, and will have seven generations of Alabama fans.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions – Don't Step On the Seal!
cards.access_notes: The seal is located on the ground at the front entrance of Langdon Hall.

cards.title: The Auburn Creed
cards.subtitle: The Moral Compass of the Plains
cards.notes: Memorize and live by the ten stanzas written by George Petrie in 1943, which define the spirit of the Auburn Family.
cards.short_summary: A foundational document outlining the values of hard work, honesty, and helpfulness that all Auburn students strive to embody.
cards.evidence_claim: Written in 1943 by George Petrie, the Creed is a unifying set of beliefs common to all Auburn students, faculty, and alumni.
cards.access_notes: The Creed is displayed in various campus buildings and celebrated annually on Creed Day.

cards.title: The Bodda Getta Chant
cards.subtitle: Nonsensical Spirit
cards.notes: Join the student section in reciting this rhythmic, fast-paced cheer that ends with a thunderous 'Auburn Tigers, Rah! Rah! Rah!'
cards.short_summary: Auburn's most famous nonsensical cheer, performed at athletic events to energize the crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bodda Getta chant was made an official cheer in the 1960s and is a favorite tradition in the student section.
cards.source_title: Get Your Hands Up for Bodda Getta!
cards.access_notes: Performed at most home athletic events, particularly football and basketball.

cards.title: Wreck Tech Pajama Parade
cards.subtitle: A Bygone Rivalry Ritual
cards.notes: Learn about the historic parade where students marched in pajamas to 'grease the tracks' before the Georgia Tech game.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued but legendary tradition where students wore pajamas to a pep rally and parade before playing Georgia Tech.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wreck Tech Parade began in the early 1930s and was a staple of the Auburn-Georgia Tech rivalry until 1987.
cards.source_title: Incredible footage from the 1983 Auburn Wreck Tech parade
cards.access_notes: This tradition is currently inactive but remains a significant part of university history.

cards.title: Ring Night & Curse Reversal
cards.subtitle: Cleansing the Class Ring
cards.notes: Dip your official class ring in the President's fountain to 'cleanse' it after tapping it on the cursed seal.
cards.short_summary: A modern tradition for juniors and seniors to celebrate receiving their official Auburn rings.
cards.evidence_claim: Part of the Ring Tradition involves 'cursing' the ring by tapping it on the Seal and 'cleansing' it in the President's fountain.
cards.access_notes: Held annually for students who have purchased the official Auburn ring.
